system.name: Cocktailer
system.one_liner: a DNN compiler that co-optimizes control flow and data flow of DNN programs in a single scheduling space for accelerators

components.name: loop
components.role: loop control flow, scheduled on the CPU separately from data-flow operators

components.name: accelerator
components.role: executes the MatMul/Add/Relu kernels launched separately from the CPU's loop

components.name: uOperator
components.role: a data-flow operator composed of independent, homogeneous uTasks

components.name: uTask
components.role: smallest scheduling unit; a homogeneous sub-task of a uOperator or a loop

components.name: uProgram
components.role: unified representation containing multiple independent uTasks, including Loop-uTasks, scheduled together

components.name: Loop-uTask
components.role: a uTask representing both the control-flow and data-flow logic of one compute unit

components.name: L0
components.role: core/thread-level parallel processing unit, the finest level of the hardware abstraction

components.name: L2-Unit
components.role: GPU device/kernel-level unit, the top of the 3-level hardware abstraction

content.key_idea: Existing DNN frameworks schedule loop control flow on the CPU separately from data-flow operator kernels on the accelerator; COCKTAILER instead unifies both into homogeneous uTasks scheduled together as a uProgram directly onto the accelerator's multi-level parallel hardware.
content.reading_order: Two side-by-side panels read top to bottom: (a) existing frameworks split the loop (CPU) from operator kernels (accelerator); (b) COCKTAILER merges them into a uProgram mapped onto L0/L1/L2 hardware units.

summary: This figure contrasts how DNN programs with control flow are executed by existing frameworks versus by COCKTAILER. In panel (a), typical frameworks such as JAX schedule the loop's control flow on the CPU while separately launching MatMul, Add, and Relu kernels on the accelerator, incurring coordination overhead between the two sides. In panel (b), COCKTAILER represents the same program as a uProgram made of homogeneous uTasks, including Loop-uTasks that carry both control-flow and data-flow logic for one compute unit; these are scheduled directly onto the accelerator's three-level hardware abstraction (L0 core, L1 SM/thread-block, L2 GPU device). The two panels share the same operator color coding (blue MatMul, yellow Relu, gray Add) so the reader can see exactly which pieces move from a CPU-side loop into accelerator-resident Loop-uTasks.
summary_zh: 该图对比传统DNN框架与COCKTAILER的执行方式：(a)现有框架将循环控制流放在CPU、算子核放在加速器上分别调度；(b)COCKTAILER将二者统一为同构uTask，组成uProgram映射到加速器三级硬件抽象执行。
